job.title: Quantity Surveyor - Power
job.description:
You won't be handed a slice of a job here. You'd own the commercial side of a project from the start to the final account.

Why this one is different

  • A main contractor in power infrastructure that is growing and hiring commercial people across several regions.
  • Cradle-to-grave ownership. You're not passing work on halfway through.
  • Private electrical networks: transformers, switchgear, HV and LV cabling. Not generic civils.
  • A hiring manager who wants someone contractually strong and trusted to challenge.

What you'd own

You'd run the commercial side of private network projects. That starts with the contract. You read it properly, find the risks and say so early. Most of the work is on NEC, so early warnings and compensation events are yours to manage, not something you hand to someone else. From there you'd run the budget and forecast, buy and pay the subcontractors, deal with variations and claims, and take the job through to final account. You'd work closely with operations, and the way you do that matters. The brief is firm but fair: you challenge decisions that put profit at risk, and you do it in a way people can work with. Negotiation is a big part of it. The aim is to get to an outcome quickly, and to know when and where it's worth pushing.

What you need

  • Contractor experience as a QS, with full commercial responsibility from award to final account.
  • Strong, practical NEC administration, including compensation events and early warnings.
  • Good contract review skills and the confidence to challenge clients, subcontractors and operations.

This suits you if you've worked in power, utilities, electrical infrastructure or civil engineering. Private networks or HV and LV experience helps, as does knowing transformers, switchgear and substations. It can be learned if you have the commercial grounding. The team also values people who are proactive, can work alone or with others, and fit the team.

The package

The base sits in the region of the market for a QS at this level, and we'll go through the numbers when we speak. A car allowance comes with the role. 25 days holiday + Bank Holidays with the option to buy/sell more. You'd be in the office around three days a week with the rest remote, based in South East London and Kent.

How it's being run

You deal with us directly. That means quick feedback and a short process: usually a 30 minute informal chat, then a more formal second stage, ideally face-to-face. You'll know where you stand at each step.

About us

We're clearnorth. We work with quantity surveyors and commercial people in construction, infrastructure and regulated utilities, perm and contract, and that's all we do. People call us the QS People. It started as a nickname and stuck because it's accurate. It's a small world, and we'll cross paths with most people reading this several times over a career, so a move that goes wrong costs us far more than it ever earns. That's why we've taken the time to understand this role properly before putting it in front of you.

The way in

We know what sending a CV out means when you're settled. Your name in the wrong inbox, your employer hearing about it second-hand, your details sat in a database you don't control. So your CV goes nowhere until we've spoken and you've said yes, and your name reaches the client only once we've agreed how. That's not us being saintly. In a world this size, one careless send and we've lost you for good, and you're worth more to us over the next twenty years than any single fee.

If the timing's not right but the role has landed, get in touch anyway. We'd rather be the people you've already met for whenever something shifts, six weeks or six years from now.

job.title: Quantity Surveyor
job.description:
About the role

A Tier 1 multi utilities contractor is hiring a Quantity Surveyor into its connections team. They work mainly across power and water, and this role sits on the ICP side, getting new developments connected to the grid.

In plain terms, if a building, site or scheme needs connecting, this is the work. New developments, EV charging infrastructure, the civils that go with it, water connections and the occasional gas connection too. Projects run from around fifty thousand pounds to half a million, so you'd carry a varied portfolio rather than babysit one slow job.

You'd report straight into the Head of Commercial and work hand in glove with the project manager, which means real visibility and no long chain to get a decision made.

The role is based in Sale, just outside Manchester, so it sits well for anyone across the North West.

What the work actually involves

This is connections work, and it moves. You own the commercial side of live schemes, manage cost against value, and keep the numbers honest as the work changes underneath you. The pace comes from the volume and the variety, several schemes at different stages, each with its own contractor conversations to have and its own margin to protect.

It also sits right in the middle of where the market is heading. Grid connections, electrification and EV infrastructure are growing, not shrinking, so the pipeline of work behind this role is the kind that builds rather than dries up.

What they actually need

Two things are non-negotiable.

You own the CVR. This isn't a monthly chore you tolerate here; it's the part of the job you're trusted to get right. They want someone who knows their numbers cold and can stand behind them.

You can negotiate to a result, fast. Connections work doesn't wait, and the commercial conversations that come with it can't sit for three weeks. They need someone who can get into a negotiation, find the outcome and close it, rather than dragging it out or hiding behind email.

Beyond that, it's about how you work. If you can manage several live schemes at once, read a contract properly and hold a firm, professional line when one's needed, you'll do well here.

It suits more backgrounds than you'd think

You don't need to have done ICP work before. Multi-utilities, civils, groundworks, main contractor and connections backgrounds all map across naturally. What matters is that you can own the commercials on a portfolio of fast-moving jobs and negotiate like you mean it.

It matters here because we've taken the time to understand this role properly rather than running commercial people through a generic process.

job.title: Quantity Surveyor
job.description:
Senior Quantity Surveyor – Power Schemes

Location: Gateshead, Newcastle upon Tyne

About the role

A Tier 1 multi-utilities contractor is hiring a Senior Quantity Surveyor to work across its power schemes in the North East.

This is a role focused on the delivery of power infrastructure projects, including but not limited to transformers, switchgear and associated civil engineering works. You'll be looking after the commercial side of these schemes from start to finish, working closely with the operational team to make sure projects are delivered profitably and the numbers stand up.

The business has an established presence in the utilities sector, with power forming a key part of its workload. You'll be joining a contractor that understands the complexities of delivering infrastructure projects and the importance of having strong commercial people involved from the outset.

You'll report directly to the Commercial Director and work closely with the project managers delivering the schemes. That means genuine involvement in decisions, direct access to senior leadership and the opportunity to influence commercial outcomes rather than simply report on them.

The role is based out of Gateshead, making it well placed for someone living in Newcastle, Sunderland, Durham or the wider North East.

What the work actually involves

This is power infrastructure work, and the commercial detail matters.

You'll take responsibility for the commercial management of live power schemes, including projects involving transformers, switchgear and the associated civils that come with delivering this type of infrastructure.

You'll be managing costs, valuations, variations and subcontractor accounts, keeping a close eye on the contractual position as projects progress.

NEC contracts are a key part of the role. You'll need to be comfortable working within the contract, managing compensation events, understanding early warnings and making sure the right commercial processes are followed as schemes develop. It's about knowing how the contract works in practice, not just recognising the terminology.

There's a mix of work to consider, with different subcontractors, programme pressures and commercial challenges to manage along the way.

You'll be expected to understand where each project stands financially, where the risks are sitting and what needs doing to protect the margin.

It's not a role where you disappear into spreadsheets and send a report at the end of the month. You'll be working alongside delivery teams, challenging costs where necessary, dealing with subcontractors and making sure the commercial position reflects what's actually happening on site.

Power infrastructure is a specialist area, and the experience you build here is experience that stays relevant. You'll be working on schemes that demand proper commercial control, sound judgement and the ability to make decisions while the work is moving.

What they actually need

Three things are non-negotiable.

You own the CVR. They need someone who can take full responsibility for cost value reconciliation, understand exactly where a project stands and explain the numbers with confidence. Not someone who simply produces a report, but someone who uses it to drive commercial decisions.

You know your way around NEC contracts. This is a key requirement. They need someone with hands-on experience administering NEC contracts, who understands compensation events, early warnings, contractual notices and the commercial implications of getting these things wrong. You'll know how to protect the contractual position without making every issue unnecessarily complicated.

You can negotiate to a result. Whether that's agreeing compensation events, managing subcontractor accounts or resolving commercial issues, they want someone who's comfortable having the conversation and getting to an outcome. Someone who can be firm when needed, pragmatic when it makes sense and doesn't let issues sit unresolved.

Beyond that, you'll need to be comfortable managing the commercial side of power and civils schemes, understanding contractual obligations and working closely with operational teams.

They want someone who takes ownership, spots problems early and knows when to challenge rather than waiting for someone else to make the call.

It suits more backgrounds than you'd think

You don't necessarily need to have spent your entire career working on power schemes.

Experience across utilities, power infrastructure, civil engineering, groundworks or major infrastructure contracting could all translate well.

What matters is that you've operated at Senior Quantity Surveyor level, have strong working knowledge of NEC contracts, understand the commercial demands of delivering infrastructure projects and can demonstrate that you've taken real ownership of the numbers.

If you've managed subcontractors, controlled costs, dealt with compensation events and protected margin on technically demanding schemes, there's a good chance your experience will be relevant.
